notes.claim: The volume of a prism is the area of its cross-section multiplied by the length.
The litre is a special name for the cubic decimetre, so a 10 cm cube (1 dm each way) is one litre.
A thousand litres make 1 m³, NIST states.
1 m³ is 1,000,000 cm³ by the same unit-cube method, so volume units scale by the cube.
Each ship tank has its own sounding table giving the volume of liquid for the whole range of sounding and ullage; sounding and ullage are distances from the bottom and from the top of the tank.
Sounding tables give tank volumes at regular intervals of liquid height in the tank.
Density is mass divided by volume; rearranged, mass is density times volume (the rearranging is arithmetic, not quoted).
Surface area is measured in square units and is built from the areas of a prism's faces, as on a net.
